name: Bullpen — Part 2
description: What actually runs at the end of Part 2: the same two Next.js apps and the same single serverless function as Part 1, with no new runtime node. What changed is that the rules I had only stated in prompts now fail a build. The controls below name the check that enforces each one: app boundaries, secret containment, the free-tier call budget, and the explorer matching this model.

nodes.name: Reader
nodes.description: A blog reader who lands on the public site to learn about Bullpen, and can now read its architecture page.

nodes.name: Player
nodes.description: A registered player who opens the trading app to view prices and (in later parts) place paper trades.

nodes.name: Bullpen Landing
nodes.description: The public landing site (apps/landing). Part 2 adds the /architecture page, which reads the repo's own records: the ADRs, the ADL, the CALM moments and the rules snapshot.

app-boundaries.description: An app never depends on another app, and imports a library only through its package entry point. Both are ADL rules that fail check:arch.

config.name: Components depend only on what they may
config.description: turbo boundaries enforces the IS DEPENDENT ON and HAS NO DEPENDENCY ON rules of structure.adl, direct and transitive, and reports a breach as the ASSERT it breaks.

config.name: Libraries are imported through their entry point
config.description: COMPONENTS use LIBRARIES ONLY THROUGH their package entry point: no @bullpen/ui/src/... and no relative path into packages/.

explorer-matches-model.description: What the architecture explorer draws has to be this model. Part 2's explorer content is checked against this file, not against the prediction.

config.name: The explorer matches the model
config.description: Every explorer node and edge exists in its CALM document, and every CALM node is drawn.

nodes.name: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.description: The trading app (apps/web) where players view live prices and will place paper trades.

app-boundaries.description: An app never depends on another app, and imports a library only through its package entry point. Both are ADL rules that fail check:arch.

config.name: Components depend only on what they may
config.description: turbo boundaries enforces the IS DEPENDENT ON and HAS NO DEPENDENCY ON rules of structure.adl, direct and transitive, and reports a breach as the ASSERT it breaks.

config.name: Libraries are imported through their entry point
config.description: COMPONENTS use LIBRARIES ONLY THROUGH their package entry point: no @bullpen/ui/src/... and no relative path into packages/.

nodes.name: Price Snapshot Service
nodes.description: Serverless function backing GET /api/price/[symbol] in apps/web; fetches a point-in-time price for a symbol from CoinGecko and returns it to the trading app. It is the only code that reads the CoinGecko Demo API key.

secret-containment.description: The CoinGecko Demo API key stays in one place: only this route reads it. Everything else in apps/ and packages/ fails check:arch if it names the variable in code.

config.name: The API key is read in one place

nodes.name: CoinGecko
nodes.description: CoinGecko's free Demo API (api.coingecko.com), called for BTC-USD price snapshots. Chosen after a Coinbase-based design was ruled out by Coinbase's Terms of Use, which forbid public display of their data (see issue #6, ADR-0005, docs/data-sources.md).

relationships.description: Reader browses the public landing site and its architecture page.
Trading app requests a live price snapshot for a symbol.
Price snapshot service calls CoinGecko's /simple/price endpoint for the current BTC-USD price, authenticated via a server-side Demo API key header, and caches the answer for 300 seconds.

attribution.description: CoinGecko's API Terms of Service require a 'Powered by CoinGecko' credit (or an approved equivalent), legible font no smaller than 10px, linked to coingecko.com, on every screen that displays the price this relationship fetches. See ADR-0005 and docs/data-sources.md.

config.name: CoinGecko attribution
config.description: apps/web's PriceCell/CoinGeckoCredit rendering satisfies this: a linked 'Powered by CoinGecko' credit next to every price sourced from this relationship.

call-budget.description: The 300 second cache interval keeps modeled monthly calls within 90% of the Demo plan's 10,000-call allowance. Lowering the interval without raising the allowance fails check:arch. See ADR-0005.

config.name: CoinGecko call budget
config.description: Modeled monthly CoinGecko calls stay within 90% of the Demo plan's monthly allowance in cost/allowances.json.

secret-containment.description: The Demo API key this call sends is read only by the route that makes the call.

config.name: The API key is read in one place
